title: Run the existing writing checkers and map protocol sections to write-task coverage
body:
## Goal
Measure, report, do not fix. Follow the recommendation in `benchmark/challenges/rows-0216.md` (section `## Recommendation`). Write one new file, `benchmark/writing/protocol-link-0217.md`. Change no other repository file. If a checker fails, record the failure and its output tail; do not repair the checker or its inputs.

Expected gain: the next shaper and the later whole-method review see whether the write extension passes its own checks and where `benchmark/protocol.md` has no write coverage. The goal requires a method covering write tasks before any write implementation. The next shaper reads `## Recommendation` in the new file.

No session can run LabVIEW. Claim no LabVIEW behaviour, native result or benchmark readiness (readiness stays false).

If the CLI answers "No such tool available: Read. Read is disabled for this session", that is a native-tool refusal, not a broker failure: propose the same operation again as a JSON action and continue (Policymaker #854). Grep matches one literal substring only.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `benchmark/writing/protocol-link-0217.md` exists with the headings `## Checker runs`, `## Protocol map`, `## Write contracts`, `## Recommendation`.
- [ ] `## Checker runs`: one table row each for `benchmark/writing/verify_method.py` and each `benchmark/writing/check_*.py` and `benchmark/writing/reviews-0128/check_integrity_0128.py`, run as `python3 -I -B <file>` (run them from the repository root), with exit code and a short output tail (at most 3 lines). If a run needs `LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT` or another unavailable input, record that as `not runnable: <reason>`, not as a pass.
- [ ] `## Protocol map`: one table row for each of the protocol sections tasks, oracle, split, baseline, challenges. Each row names the writing artifact (file:line) that extends it or says `absent`.
- [ ] `## Write contracts`: for each of WC1, WM1, WM2, WB1 (`benchmark/writing/README.md:15-18`) and the WP1 text case, state whether an independent key exists (file name) and what blocks it (native capability, owner material, or nothing), citing file:line.
- [ ] `## Recommendation`: one next task needing no LabVIEW, owner material or product code, with its expected gain and a verification command; or a concrete statement that the remaining write gaps all need native capability or the owner.
- [ ] No `__pycache__` under `benchmark/`.

## Verification
python3 -c "import pathlib; t=pathlib.Path('benchmark/writing/protocol-link-0217.md').read_text(); L=t.splitlines(); assert all(h in L for h in ('## Checker runs','## Protocol map','## Write contracts','## Recommendation')); assert all(s in t for s in ('verify_method.py','tasks','oracle','split','baseline','challenges','WC1','WM1','WM2','WB1','WP1')); assert not list(pathlib.Path('benchmark').rglob('__pycache__')); print('OK')"

## Context
- `benchmark/challenges/rows-0216.md` (#924 iteration 0216): all EV:63-68 rows PARTIAL; write tasks exist only as unexecuted design. Its recommendation is this task.
- `benchmark/writing/README.md:37` documents `verify_method.py`.
- Do not check changes with `git status` (the worker directory is not a git repository). Check outputs by reading the file. Do not run `git commit`; the parent commits.
- Do not re-survey: `benchmark/challenges/next-gap-0202.md`, `reader-integration-0212.md`, the scorer-intake thread.

## Budget
Read: `benchmark/challenges/rows-0216.md` (whole); `benchmark/writing/README.md` (whole); `benchmark/protocol.md` (headings plus the lines you cite; Read in ranges); `benchmark/project-text-writing-0109.md` (lines you cite). Glob `benchmark/writing/` for names. Do not read whole key/review JSON files; open only the head or the fields you cite. Keep command output short (tails only). Report early: write the new file by about turn 25, then refine.
